sources.claim: About 1.89 million seafarers serve the world merchant fleet.
sources.title: World shipping faces looming officer shortage (Marine Log, 28 July 2021)
sources.quote: The report estimates that 1.89 million seafarers currently serve the world merchant fleet, operating over 74,000 vessels
sources.note: The 1.89 million figure is from the 2021 BIMCO/ICS report, read here through press coverage. BIMCO's own page now describes a 2026 edition (25 June 2026) whose figures were not readable from this environment. Do not call this the latest estimate.

sources.claim: Sea-based Filipino workers sent home 7.139 billion US dollars in 2025.
sources.title: OFW remittances hit record $35.6B (BusinessWorld, reporting Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas data)
sources.quote: remittances from sea-based OFWs rose by 2.9% to $7.139 billion in 2025 from $6.941 billion in 2024
sources.note: Secondary report of BSP data. The BSP page itself returned 403 to this environment.

sources.claim: About 3.7 million bitcoin, around 20 percent of supply, had not moved for at least five years in June 2020. Dormancy is a proxy for lost, not proof of lost keys.
sources.title: Lost Bitcoin: 3.7 million Bitcoin are probably gone forever (Decrypt)
sources.quote: According to a June 2020 report by blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, around 3.7 million BTC
sources.published: 2020 (exact article date not shown in page text)
sources.note: Chainalysis blog post itself not located (guessed URLs returned 404). Press coverage only. Describe as dormant for five years, never as confirmed lost keys.

sources.claim: The same coverage puts this at around 20 percent of minted bitcoin.
